answer.text: Minority investors to block any sale transaction
The shareholder holding the right to require the subject shareholders (for example, promoters) to sell to the same buyer on the same terms
The custodian to sell fund assets
Investors to redeem units at any time

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines drag-along as an obligation on the subject shareholders to sell to a potential purchaser when the shareholder holding the drag-along right chooses to sell. The example given is a minority AIF investor that can drag the promoters to the same buyer on the same terms, enabling a clean 100% exit. The Trap: Drag-along is not inherently a majority-over-minority tool — in the workbook's example it is the minority AIF investor that holds the right. The shareholder with the right pulls the subject shareholders into the sale on identical terms, regardless of who is in the majority. Note: Rewrote the keyed option to match the workbook's framing (the holder of the right drags the subject shareholders), because the original majority-over-minority wording is not the workbook's framing. Drag-along still refers to the same exit-coordination concept.
